items.solution_latex: Separate: \frac{dy}{y} = 3dx. Integrate: \ln|y| = 3x + C. Exponentiate: y = A e^{3x}. Apply y(0) = 4: A = 4. Final answer: y = 4 e^{3x}.
hint_ladder: Don't forget to include the constant of integration after integration.
Apply the initial condition only after finding the general solution.
items.targets_because: This item emphasizes the importance of including the constant of integration during the integration step.

items.solution_latex: Separate: \frac{dy}{y} = 5x dx. Integrate: \ln|y| = \frac{5}{2}x^2 + C. Exponentiate: y = A e^{\frac{5}{2}x^2}. Apply y(1) = 3: 3 = A e^{\frac{5}{2}} \Rightarrow A = 3 e^{-\frac{5}{2}}. Final answer: y = 3 e^{-\frac{5}{2}} e^{\frac{5}{2}x^2}.
hint_ladder: Remember to include the constant of integration after integrating both sides.
Use the initial condition after obtaining the general solution.
items.targets_because: This item requires the student to integrate correctly while emphasizing the necessity of the constant of integration.

items.solution_latex: Separate: \frac{dy}{y} = 6dx. Integrate: \ln|y| = 6x + C. Exponentiate: y = A e^{6x}. Apply y(2) = 10: 10 = A e^{12} \Rightarrow A = 10 e^{-12}. Final answer: y = 10 e^{-12} e^{6x}.
hint_ladder: Don't forget the constant of integration after integration.

items.solution_latex: Separate: \frac{dy}{y^2} = 4dx. Integrate: -\frac{1}{y} = 4x + C. Rearrange: y = -\frac{1}{4x + C}. Apply y(1) = 1: 1 = -\frac{1}{4 + C} \Rightarrow C = -5. Final answer: y = -\frac{1}{4x - 5}.
hint_ladder: Remember to integrate both sides before applying the initial condition.
Ensure you include the constant of integration during the integration process.
items.targets_because: This extension item challenges the student to apply the concept of integration constants in a different context, reinforcing the necessity of +C.
